stories.title: Aughinish Alumina warns sanctions would impact power grid
stories.summary: Aughinish Alumina, the refinery in Co Limerick at the centre of a controversy over its raw material allegedly ending up in Russian weapons, has warned the Government that any attempt to sanction its sale of alumina to Moscow would have implications for Ireland's national gas and electricity grids. The document states that Aughinish Alumina "exports excess electricity to the national grid, enough to power [circa] 200,000 Irish households". The note also warns that Aughinish provides up to €25m each year for the maintenance of the natural gas grid. In such a scenario, the company warns, the Government would have to pick up the tab for what Aughinish currently provides towards the maintenance of the national gas grid.

stories.summary: NATO stands "ready to defend every inch ⁠of its territory", the alliance's chief Mark Rutte has said, after a drone hit an apartment building in member state Romania ‌during ⁠an overnight Russian attack on neighbouring Ukraine. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Mr Rutte said in ‌a post on X. "Last night showed ⁠yet again that ‌the implications of their illegal war of ⁠aggression ‌don't stop at the border." "We will continue to strengthen our deterrence ⁠and defence at home and ⁠continue our support for Ukraine as they defend against Russia's aggression," he added. Mr Rutte's comments come after two people were wounded in the drone strike on an apartment building near the Ukrainian border in Romania, its defence ministry said.

stories.title: Blue Origin rocket explodes on launch pad in Florida
stories.summary: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded during a test on the launch pad in Cape Canaveral, Florida, but officials said no injuries were reported from the incident. "We experienced an anomaly during today's hotfire test," the company said in a brief statement posted to X. Video from the incident showed smoke emerging from beneath the rocket - which stood 98 metres tall - before it fully combusted into a massive fireball. The explosion is the latest setback for the space exploration company owned by billionaire Jeff Bezos and the New Glenn rocket is at the heart of the company's space ambitions.

stories.title: 'Significant delays' expected after DART suspension
stories.summary: Iarnród Éireann has said it expects "significant delays" and alterations to the DART and other suburban trains after a "major" signal fault led to a suspension of services. A spokesperson for the company said the fault affecting the network has been rectified. The issue was caused by a central computer signalling fault, but trains are moving again. The fault impacted all DART and Northern Commuter train services, as well as Phoenix Park Tunnel, Rosslare and Sligo services.

stories.title: Post-mortem to take place after woman found dead
stories.summary: Gardaí are appealing for information ahead of a post-mortem examination after a woman was found dead in Co Galway yesterday. Masuma Sohrabi's body was discovered near an IPAS accommodation centre by Waterloo Bridge, on the outskirts of Clifden, shortly before 9am yesterday. A man in his 30s was arrested yesterday and is receiving medical treatment. A post-mortem examination on Ms Sohrabi's body is due to take place today.

stories.title: Lynch family vow to campaign on enforcement of scrambler bike law
stories.summary: The parents of teenager Grace Lynch, who died in January after being hit by a scrambler bike, have said they plan to campaign to ensure the laws enacted in memory of their daughter are properly enforced by An Garda Síochána. Grace Lynch, 16, died after she was struck at a pedestrian crossing on the Rathoath Road in Finglas on 25 January this year. New regulations introduced in April ban the use of scramblers and similar off-road vehicles in public places and provide gardaí with expanded powers to seize and destroy them. Asked what the introduction of the law meant to her family, Grace’s mother Siobhán said "it meant a legacy for Grace... that she’ll always be remembered".
